culture.textEn: To call a server in a restaurant, people often say {ko:여기요} (over here). It does not point to age or rank, so it suits any server.

sources.title: 호칭을 정해주세요. (Please settle on forms of address), an Online Ganada answer
sources.publisher: 국립국어원 (National Institute of Korean Language), 온라인가나다 (Online Ganada)
sources.quoteOrLocator: Answer of 2025-12-22, quoting the institute's guide 「우리, 뭐라고 부를까요?」, section [직원과 손님을 부르거나 이르는 말]: “식당, 미용실, 상점과 같은 서비스 기관의 직원을 부르는 말로 ‘여기요’, ‘저기요’ 등이 이미 보편적으로 사용되고 있습니다. 이 말은 직원과 손님 사이라는 사회적 관계를 직접 드러내지 않는다는 점에서 손님과 직원 모두에게 편안하게 사용되고 있습니다.”

sources.title: [카드뉴스] 헷갈리고 궁금했던 호칭‧지칭어, 정리해드립니다! (card news by the 대학생기자단 student reporters, 2020-06-01)
sources.publisher: 문화체육관광부 (Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism), student-reporter card news; cards marked ⓒ국립국어원
sources.quoteOrLocator: Body text: “식당이나 상점과 같은 서비스 직종의 직원을 부르게 된다면 ‘여기요’, ‘저기요’라는 표현이 적절합니다.” Card image text (alt): “‘여기요’, ‘저기요’는 직원과 손님 사이의 사회적 관계를 드러내지 않는 호칭입니다.”

verification.notes:
Line 1 (pass 2, author sourcing, 2026-10-14): both pages fetched; the NIKL Online Ganada answer quotes the institute's own address guide: 여기요 and 저기요 are already in common use to call staff at restaurants, salons and shops, and are comfortable for both sides because they do not show the customer-staff relationship; the MCST card news (student reporters, NIKL cards) calls them appropriate for service staff and says they do not show a social relationship. The note says 'often', makes no group-wide claim and restates the passages in new English words. Carried by: q1 Discover page 2 word note, q1 apply prompt t1, the gloss of 여기요.
Line 2 (pass 2b, independent fact check, 2026-10-14): both pages re-fetched by a session that did not author the cell; the NIKL Online Ganada answer of 2025-12-22 says 여기요 and 저기요 are already in common use to call staff at restaurants, salons and shops and do not directly show the customer-staff relationship, and the MCST card news (cards marked NIKL) calls them fitting for service staff and puts treating a person as a person ahead of age or social standing; 'often' and 'does not point to age or rank' match both. No wording copied. Outcome: pass, unchanged.
Line 3 (pass 5, MAR culture review, 2026-10-14): both pages re-fetched; each quoteOrLocator is on its page as quoted; 'often' and 'does not point to age or rank' match the NIKL guide and the MCST card news; no group-wide claim, no wording copied, no designation number, no real person, shop, brand or price. Outcome: pass, unchanged.

culture.textEn: Some people say {ko:잘 먹겠습니다} (I will eat well) just before they start a meal. No rule settles whether saying it is right or wrong.

sources.title: Online Ganada question and answer on the meal phrase, titled 잘먹겠습니다
sources.publisher: 국립국어원 (National Institute of Korean Language), 온라인가나다 (Online Ganada)
sources.quoteOrLocator: Answer [식사 인사] of 2026-01-13: “이에 대해서 규정으로 정해 놓은 것은 없습니다. 따라서 무엇이 맞고 틀리다고 말씀드리기는 어렵습니다. 제시하신 상황에서 ‘잘 먹겠습니다’처럼 쓰는 것이 틀렸다고 볼 만한 근거는 딱히 없어 보입니다.”

sources.title: 밥상 앞 “잘 먹겠습니다”, 밥값 내달란 말로 들리시나요? [넷만세]
sources.quoteOrLocator: Lead paragraph: “밥이 차려진 식탁 앞에서 숟가락을 들기 전 하는 말 ‘잘 먹겠습니다’. 사람에 따라서 자주 쓰기도 하는 이 말이 …” and closing paragraph: “우리말에서 ‘잘 먹겠습니다’라는 표현이 자주 쓰이게 된 시기나 유래에 대해서는 정확히 알려진 바 없다.”

verification.notes:
Line 1 (pass 2, author sourcing, 2026-10-14): both pages fetched; the newspaper describes the phrase as what is said at a laid table before lifting the spoon, used often by some people, with views differing on when it fits; the NIKL Online Ganada answer says no rule governs it and there is no ground to call it wrong. The note says 'many people', avoids any claim about origin, about who pays or about everyone, and copies no wording. Carried by: q3 Discover page 3 word note and gloss, q3 apply turn 1, q3 check c1 option.
Line 2 (pass 2b, independent fact check, 2026-10-14): both pages re-fetched by a session that did not author the cell; the NIKL answer of 2026-01-13 says no rule settles the matter, so right or wrong is hard to say, and finds no clear ground to call the phrase wrong in the situation asked about; the newspaper says some people use it often and reports differing views. Two overstatements fixed: 'never wrong to say it' (the institute only found no clear ground, and the article reports people who disagree) became 'No rule settles whether saying it is right or wrong', and 'Many people' (not quantified by either source) became 'Some people', here and in the q3 word note with its es and ko overlays. No wording copied. Outcome: fixed.
Line 3 (pass 5, MAR culture review, 2026-10-14): both pages re-fetched; the quotes are on their pages; the note now says 'Some people' (Line 1's 'many people' was fixed in Line 2) and that no rule settles it, as NIKL and the newspaper say; the q3 Discover adds the server exchange (맛있게 드세요 / 잘 먹겠습니다) as one option some people use, so the game models it, the note hedges it. No origin, payer or everyone claim; no wording copied. Outcome: pass.

culture.textEn: Korean money is counted in won ({ko:원}). Amounts are read with the numbers {ko:이} (two), {ko:삼} (three) and {ko:천} (thousand), so {ko:이천 원} is 2,000 won.

sources.title: 원 (Standard Korean Language Dictionary entry 원 1, dependent noun)
sources.publisher: 표준국어대사전 (Standard Korean Language Dictionary), National Institute of Korean Language
sources.quoteOrLocator: Entry 원 1 「의존 명사」: “우리나라의 화폐 단위. 1원은 1전의 100배이다. 1962년 6월 10일부터 시행되었다. 기호는 ￦.”

sources.title: 원, an entry of the Encyclopedia of Korean Culture
sources.publisher: 한국민족문화대백과사전 (Encyclopedia of Korean Culture), Academy of Korean Studies
sources.quoteOrLocator: Entry 원, 정의: “우리나라에서 1962년 6월 12일에 단행된 통화개혁 이래로 오늘날까지 사용되고 있는 화폐단위.”

sources.title: 천 (Standard Korean Language Dictionary entry 천 3, numeral)
sources.publisher: 표준국어대사전 (Standard Korean Language Dictionary), National Institute of Korean Language
sources.quoteOrLocator: Entry 천 3 (千) [Ⅰ]「수사」: “백의 열 배가 되는 수.” The same dictionary, entry 이 7 (二/貳) 「수사」: “일에 일을 더한 수.”, and entry 삼 6 (三) 「수사」: “이에 일을 더한 수.”

verification.notes:
Line 1 (pass 2, author sourcing, 2026-10-14): the three pages fetched; the dictionary defines 원 as the country's currency unit, the encyclopedia as the currency unit used since the 1962 currency reform to this day (the two sources give June 10 and June 12 for the date; the note states no date); the dictionary's numeral entries give 천 as a thousand and 이, 삼 as two and three, the Sino-Korean numerals (hanja 千, 二, 三). Prices in the cell are round practice amounts in a drawn menu (OD-11), no shop, brand or product price. Carried by: q3 Discover page 1 caption and key words, q3 practice and check rounds, the menu realia values.
Line 2 (pass 2b, independent fact check, 2026-10-14): the dictionary entries 원 1, 천 3, 이 7 and 삼 6 and the Encyclopedia of Korean Culture entry 원 re-fetched by a session that did not author the cell; 원 is the country's currency unit (the encyclopedia: in use since the 1962 reform), and 이, 삼, 천 are the numerals two, three and a thousand, so 이천 원 reads 2,000 won. The note states no date, so the June 10 and June 12 difference does not touch it. No wording copied. Outcome: pass, unchanged.
Line 3 (pass 5, MAR culture review, 2026-10-14): the dictionary entries 원 1, 천 3, 이 7, 삼 6 and the encyclopedia entry 원 re-fetched; quotes verbatim; the note states no date, so the June 10 / June 12 difference does not touch it; prices are round practice amounts on a drawn menu, no shop, brand or product price; no wording copied. Outcome: pass, unchanged.

culture.textEn: Before a counter such as {ko:개}, one, two and three are said {ko:한}, {ko:두} and {ko:세}, as in {ko:두 개} (two things).

sources.title: 한 (Standard Korean Language Dictionary entry 한 1, determiner)
sources.publisher: 표준국어대사전 (Standard Korean Language Dictionary), National Institute of Korean Language
sources.quoteOrLocator: Entry 한 1 「관형사」 「1」: “그 수량이 하나임을 나타내는 말.”

sources.title: 두 (Standard Korean Language Dictionary entry 두 1, determiner)
sources.publisher: 표준국어대사전 (Standard Korean Language Dictionary), National Institute of Korean Language
sources.quoteOrLocator: Entry 두 1 「관형사」: “그 수량이 둘임을 나타내는 말.”

sources.title: 세 and 개 (Standard Korean Language Dictionary entries 세 1 and 개 7)
sources.publisher: 표준국어대사전 (Standard Korean Language Dictionary), National Institute of Korean Language
sources.quoteOrLocator: Entry 세 1 「관형사」: “그 수량이 셋임을 나타내는 말.” Entry 개 7 (個/箇/介) 「의존 명사」 「1」 (searchKeyword=개): “낱으로 된 물건을 세는 단위.”

verification.notes:
Line 1 (pass 2, author sourcing, 2026-10-14): the dictionary result pages fetched; 한, 두, 세 are determiners meaning a quantity of one, two and three (하나, 둘, 셋), used before a noun or counter, and 개 is the counter for single things. The cell never pairs 네 (four) with 개 because 네 is also 'yes'. Carried by: q2 Discover page 2 caption and word notes, q2 practice options, q2 apply and check lines.
Line 2 (pass 2b, independent fact check, 2026-10-14): the dictionary entries 한 1, 두 1, 세 1 (determiners: a quantity of one, two, three) and 개 7 (the counter for single things) re-fetched by a session that did not author the cell; they support the short forms before a counter and the example 두 개. No wording copied. Outcome: pass, unchanged.
Line 3 (pass 5, MAR culture review, 2026-10-14): the entries 한 1, 두 1, 세 1 and 개 7 re-fetched and verbatim; they define 한, 두, 세 as determiners for a quantity of one, two, three, not a 'short form' rule, so the note was reworded to state only what they say: before a counter such as 개, one, two and three are said 한, 두, 세 (no other source stating the rule was found). No wording copied. Outcome: fixed.

notes: Language pass 4 (MAR): spelling, spacing, register and romanization clean; applied Discover exchanges for the server lines (뭐 드릴까요?, 라면 하나요?, 삼천 원이에요, 맛있게 드세요), offers without -도, taught 잘 가요 for the 안녕히 가세요 distractor, counter notes in the right direction, 'One bowl of instant noodles?', 네, 얼마예요?; kept the q3 Check reply round.

Culture pass 5 (MAR): all sources re-fetched (verification line 3); n4 reworded to what the dictionary says; 잘 먹겠습니다 modelled as one option some people use; milk kept on the drawn menu; no real person, shop, brand or price; no all-Koreans claim; no age wording.
